subject: maths
title: Free-Fall Falls
description: Analyse vertical motion under gravity g ≈ 9.81 m/s².

concepts.def: Near Earth's surface g ≈ 9.81 m/s² downward (use 9.8 in many UK exams).
Choose upward positive: a = −g. Choose downward positive: a = +g.
u=0, falls with a=g; v = gt, s = ½gt².
u>0 upward, decelerates, momentarily stops, then falls.
At top v = 0, so t_peak = u/g.
Often ignored at A-Level for simplicity.

walkthroughs.h2: Drop from rest 20 m: time to land?
walkthroughs.body_html:
s = ½gt²

20 = ½·9.8 t² → t² = 4.082 t ≈ 2.02 s

walkthroughs.h2: Ball thrown up at 19.6 m/s, max height
walkthroughs.body_html:
v² = u² − 2gs, v=0 at top

s = u²/(2g) = 384.16/19.6 = 19.6 m

If you divide both sides of an inequality by -2, what happens to the inequality sign?
options: The inequality becomes an equals sign.
The inequality sign stays the same — you treat it like an equation.
The inequality sign reverses (e.g. > becomes <).
The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of (3x + 1)^2 with respect to x?
options: The derivative is 2(3x + 1) — applying the power rule without the chain rule.
6(3x + 1) — by the chain rule, multiplying by the derivative of the inside (3).
The inequality becomes an equals sign.
The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.

mcqs.q: What is 0.00307 written to 2 significant figures?
options: The inequality becomes an equals sign.
0.0031 — leading zeros are not significant; the first two significant figures are 3 and 0.
0.003, treating significant figures the same as decimal places.
0.00 — counting the first two digits after the decimal point.
